title: The Long Protocol
premise: Zephyrine Coldharbour, a navigator who fled his past by hauling cargo through contested orbits, receives a distress signal broadcast in Vessic, the extinct tongue of the colony he was born in—and of the backup copies of himself sleeping in his hold, which he has never dared wake. The signal comes from a relay at the edge of dead space where someone is using his own stolen memories as a key, and the only way to silence it is to answer it in person. Racing a closing jump window, pursued by a salvage syndicate that wants the backups and a former partner who wants the truth, Zephyrine discovers the signal was sent by his own first backup, who has been awake for years and remembers the massacre Zephyrine ran from. In the relay's heart, he must choose between destroying the copies to keep his identity singular and intact, or merging with what he abandoned—choosing belonging over the comfortable lie of being no one—and the book ends with him opening the jump window not to escape, but to bring the lost Vessic colony's survivors home.
about_author: Astrid Delacroix is the pen name of a former maritime radio operator who spent a decade listening to frequencies no one answered, and now writes about the people who do. They live in a coastal town where the fog comes in like weather from another story.

chapters.title: Cargo of Sleepers
chapters.summary: Zephyrine's POV. A routine haul through contested orbits establishes his careful invisibility and the sealed hold he never opens. Emotional beat: controlled loneliness, the cost of a life built on not being noticed.

chapters.title: The Frequency That Shouldn't Exist
chapters.summary: Zephyrine's POV. A distress signal arrives in Vessic, a language extinct two centuries—except to him. He almost deletes it. Emotional beat: dread curdling into recognition.

chapters.title: Ten Years Invisible
chapters.summary: Zephyrine's POV, flashback woven in. How he bought a ship, falsified his registry, and buried his name. Emotional beat: the ache of a self amputated to survive.

chapters.title: Answering Machine
chapters.summary: Zephyrine's POV. He replies in Vessic on a private channel and the signal stops—then resumes, addressed to him by his birth name. Emotional beat: terror of being seen.

chapters.title: Passengers at Dock Nine
chapters.summary: Third person, dockmaster Ilsa Voss. A salvage syndicate crew arrives asking after ships that received anomalous signals. Emotional beat: the net tightening around a man who thought no one was looking.

chapters.title: The Hold He Never Opens
chapters.summary: Zephyrine's POV. He inspects the backup cradles for the first time in years: six sleepers with his face. Emotional beat: shame and vertigo—his past literally sleeping behind a bulkhead.

chapters.title: Old Debt, Old Name
chapters.summary: Zephyrine's POV. His former partner Sef Calloway tracks him down, wanting a piece of whatever the syndicate is hunting. Emotional beat: loyalty as a leash he thought he'd cut.

chapters.title: The Jump Window
chapters.summary: Zephyrine's POV. Navigation math shows one viable corridor to the dead-space relay before it closes in nineteen days. Emotional beat: resolve forming against his own instincts.

chapters.title: Running Dark
chapters.summary: Zephyrine's POV. He slips his moorings and burns cold through a customs cordon. Emotional beat: the strange freedom of finally being a fugitive on purpose.

chapters.title: Sef Boards
chapters.summary: Sef's POV. Sef stows away, forces a reckoning: he knows what Zephyrine fled, and what's in the hold. Emotional beat: betrayal and old affection tangled together.

chapters.title: Terms of Silence
chapters.summary: Zephyrine and Sef, alternating. They negotiate an uneasy alliance—Sef's silence for a share of whatever the relay holds. Emotional beat: trust as a transaction neither believes in.

chapters.title: Signal Anatomy
chapters.summary: Zephyrine's POV. He decodes the signal's structure and finds it uses his own childhood memories as an encryption key. Emotional beat: violation—someone has been inside his head.

chapters.title: The Syndicate's Wake
chapters.summary: Third person, syndicate hunter Brann Oduya. Oduya backtraces the private channel and sets course. Emotional beat: patient, professional menace.

chapters.title: Dead Space Rules
chapters.summary: Zephyrine's POV. Entering the dead zone: no beacons, no rescue, comms dying one band at a time. Emotional beat: isolation sharpening into clarity.

chapters.title: What the Backups Dream
chapters.summary: Zephyrine's POV. Telemetry from the cradles shows REM activity—someone or something is pinging the sleepers. Emotional beat: the past is not asleep after all.

chapters.title: Sef's Version
chapters.summary: Sef's POV. Sef recalls the night of the Vessic evacuation and what Zephyrine actually did—something nobler and more damning than running. Emotional beat: loyalty to a memory versus loyalty to the man.

chapters.title: The Relay at the Edge
chapters.summary: Zephyrine's POV. First sight of the ancient Vessic relay station, lit and breathing, impossibly maintained. Emotional beat: awe curdling into suspicion.

chapters.title: Docking With a Ghost
chapters.summary: Zephyrine's POV. The station docks his ship without being asked. Emotional beat: helplessness—the hunter becomes the cargo.

chapters.title: The First Backup
chapters.summary: Zephyrine's POV. He meets Vess-1, his first backup, awake for six years, who sent the signal. Emotional beat: meeting the self he refused to be.

chapters.title: Two of One Nothing
chapters.summary: Vess-1's POV. The backup's account of waking alone, learning the language, and choosing Zephyrine as the only person worth calling. Emotional beat: loneliness mirrored and doubled.

chapters.title: The Massacre, Told Twice
chapters.summary: Alternating Zephyrine and Vess-1. Their memories of the Vessic colony's destruction diverge—and the backup's is more accurate. Emotional beat: identity as a story you tell to survive.

chapters.title: Oduya Arrives
chapters.summary: Oduya's POV. The syndicate ship enters dead space, running the same corridor. Emotional beat: the outside world refusing to stay outside.

chapters.title: Why the Signal Was Sent
chapters.summary: Vess-1's POV. The relay holds a dormant colony ship of Vessic survivors in cold sleep, keyed to a living navigator's memories—Zephyrine's. Emotional beat: the weight of being someone's only key.

chapters.title: Sef Makes a Call
chapters.summary: Sef's POV. Cornered by the syndicate's approach, Sef transmits their position, believing it will save them all. Emotional beat: betrayal committed out of love.

chapters.title: Confrontation in the Cradle Bay
chapters.summary: Zephyrine's POV. Zephyrine finds Sef at the transmitter; the argument that was ten years coming finally happens. Emotional beat: truth as a weapon and a wound.

chapters.title: The Syndicate's Offer
chapters.summary: Zephyrine's POV. Oduya, boarded and armed, offers Zephyrine the backups' market price and a clean slate. Emotional beat: temptation of the comfortable lie, again.

chapters.title: What a Copy Owes the Original
chapters.summary: Vess-1's POV. Vess-1 offers the alternative: merge the memory cores, wake the colonists, and stop being singular. Emotional beat: belonging offered at the price of self.

chapters.title: Sabotage
chapters.summary: Third person, Oduya. Oduya's crew begins stripping the relay's jump-couplings, which will seal the corridor with everyone inside. Emotional beat: greed as an extinction event.

chapters.title: The Window Starts Closing
chapters.summary: Zephyrine's POV. Navigation readouts: hours, not days. He must choose—fight, flee, or open the colony ship now. Emotional beat: panic compressed into purpose.

chapters.title: Sef's Redemption Run
chapters.summary: Sef's POV. Sef takes the syndicate's fire onto himself to buy Zephyrine time at the coupling controls. Emotional beat: loyalty finally paid in truth and blood.

chapters.title: The Key Turns
chapters.summary: Zephyrine's POV. He feeds the relay his unedited memories—the ones he's spent ten years hiding from—and the colony ship begins to wake. Emotional beat: identity surrendered as an offering, not a loss.

chapters.title: Waking Vessic
chapters.summary: Alternating POVs. Colonists stir; the first voice on the open channel is a child asking a question in Vessic. Emotional beat: grief and homecoming in the same breath.

chapters.title: Oduya's Last Bargain
chapters.summary: Oduya's POV. Facing two hundred witnesses and no market, Oduya tries to take the ship by force and fails. Emotional beat: the invisible man, seen by everyone, is unstealable.

chapters.title: The Merge
chapters.summary: Zephyrine and Vess-1. In the relay's core, Zephyrine chooses integration over deletion, taking the backup's six years of grief into himself. Emotional beat: the self expanded, not erased.

chapters.title: One Navigator, Whole
chapters.summary: Zephyrine's POV. He wakes with two lifetimes of memory and plots the corridor home through dead space. Emotional beat: quiet, earned wholeness.

chapters.title: Burials in Vacuum
chapters.summary: Zephyrine's POV. They bury Sef and the syndicate dead according to Vessic rite, in the language everyone can now speak. Emotional beat: mourning as belonging.

chapters.title: The Long Protocol
chapters.summary: Zephyrine's POV. The colony ship's crew explains the protocol he was named for: the standing order that no Vessic navigator be left alone. Emotional beat: the revelation that he was never meant to be invisible.

chapters.title: Contested Orbit, Contested Self
chapters.summary: Zephyrine's POV. Returning through the customs cordon, he files his real name for the first time in ten years. Emotional beat: fear and relief indistinguishable.

chapters.title: Cargo of Wakers
chapters.summary: Zephyrine's POV. He takes the colonists as his first honest cargo, the hold's sleepers finally awake and walking his decks. Emotional beat: the ship, and the man, repurposed.

chapters.title: Home Is a Heading
chapters.summary: Zephyrine's POV. Epilogue: he sets course for the old Vessic system with the survivors, the window open ahead. Emotional beat: belonging chosen, not found—endings as beginnings.
